<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">84</p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU3"></a><a name="GLOSSARY_OIL_NATURAL_GAS_TERMS"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="GLOSSARY_OIL_NATURAL_GAS_TERMS"></a>GLOSSARY OF OIL AND</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> NATURAL GAS TERMS</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following are abbreviations and definitions of certain terms used in this document, which are commonly used in the oil and natural gas industry:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3-D seismic: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Geophysical data that depict the subsurface strata in three dimensions. 3-D seismic typically provides a more detailed and accurate interpretation of the subsurface strata than 2-D, or two-dimensional, seismic.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basin: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A large natural depression on the earth&#8217;s surface in which sediments generally brought by water accumulate.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bbl: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One stock tank barrel of 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume used herein in reference to crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bcf: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One billion cubic feet of natural gas.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Boe: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One barrel of oil equivalent, calculated by converting natural gas to oil equivalent barrels at a ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of oil. This is an energy content correlation and does not reflect a value or price relationship between the commodities.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Boe/d: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One Boe per day.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">British thermal unit or Btu: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a one-pound mass of water from 58.5 to 59.5 degrees Fahrenheit.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Completion: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Installation of permanent equipment for production of oil or gas, or, in the case of a dry well, to reporting to the appropriate authority that the well has been abandoned.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Condensate: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A mixture of hydrocarbons that exists in the gaseous phase at original reservoir temperature and pressure, but that, when produced, is in the liquid phase at surface pressure and temperature.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Delineation: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The process of placing a number of wells in various parts of a reservoir to determine its boundaries and production characteristics.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Developed acreage: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The number of acres that are allocated or assignable to productive wells or wells capable of production.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Development costs: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Costs incurred to obtain access to proved reserves and to provide facilities for extracting, treating, gathering and storing the oil and natural gas. For a complete definition of development costs refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(7).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Development project: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The means by which petroleum resources are brought to the status of economically producible. As examples, the development of a single reservoir or field, an incremental development in a producing field or the integrated development of a group of several fields and associated facilities with a common ownership may constitute a development project.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Development well: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Differential: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">An adjustment to the price of oil or natural gas from an established spot market price to reflect differences in the quality and/or location of oil or natural gas.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Downspacing: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Additional wells drilled between known producing wells to better develop the reservoir.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dry well: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A well found to be incapable of producing hydrocarbons in sufficient quantities such that proceeds from the sale of such production exceed production expenses and taxes.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Economically producible: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The term economically producible, as it relates to a resource, means a resource which generates revenue that exceeds, or is reasonably expected to exceed, the costs of the operation. For a complete definition of economically producible, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(10).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Estimated ultimate recovery or EUR: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The sum of reserves remaining as of a given date and cumulative production as of that date.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Exploratory well: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or natural gas in another reservoir.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU4"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fiel</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">d: </font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on, or related to, the same individual geological structural feature or stratigraphic condition. The field name refers to the surface area, although it may refer to both the sur</font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">face and the underground productive formations. For a complete definition of field, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(15).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Formation: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A layer of rock which has distinct characteristics that differs from nearby rock.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Generation 1: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;&#160;With respect to our Eagle Ford Acreage, a hybrid fracking technique using approximately 1,500 pounds per foot of sand and 33 Bbls per foot of fluid, with 200 foot stages and five clusters per stage at 80 barrels per minute. With respect to our North Louisiana Acreage, a slickwater fracking technique using approximately 1,450 pounds per foot of sand, with 200 foot stages and one cluster per stage at 57 barrels per minute.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Generation 3: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">With respect to our Eagle Ford Acreage, a slickwater fracking technique using approximately 3,700 pounds per foot of sand and 75 Bbls per foot of fluid, with 150 foot stages and nine clusters per stage at 90 barrels per minute.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gross acres or gross wells: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The total acres or wells, as the case may be, in which a working interest is owned.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Held by production: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Acreage covered by a mineral lease that perpetuates a company&#8217;s right to operate a property as long as the property produces a minimum paying quantity of oil or gas.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Horizontal drilling: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;&#160;A drilling technique used in certain formations where a well is drilled vertically to a certain depth and then drilled at a right angle within a specified interval.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">MBbls: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One thousand barrels of crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">MBoe: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#160;&#160;One thousand Boe.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mcf: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One thousand cubic feet of natural gas.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">MMBbls: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One million barrels of crude oil, condensate or NGLs.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">MMBoe: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One million Boe.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">MMBtu: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">One million British thermal units.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net acres or net wells: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Gross acres or wells, as the case may be, multiplied by our working interest ownership percentage.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net production: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Production that is owned less royalties and production due to others.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NGLs: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Natural gas liquids. Hydrocarbons found in natural gas which may be extracted as liquefied petroleum gas and natural gasoline.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NYMEX: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The New York Mercantile Exchange.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Offset operator: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Any entity that has an active lease on an adjoining property for oil, natural gas or NGLs purposes.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operator: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The individual or company responsible for the development and/or production of an oil or natural gas well or lease.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Play: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A geographic area with hydrocarbon potential.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Possible Reserves: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Reserves that are less certain to be recovered than probable reserves.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Present value of future net revenues or PV-10: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The estimated future gross revenue to be generated from the production of proved reserves, net of estimated production and future development and abandonment costs, using prices and costs in effect at the determination date, before income taxes, and without giving effect to non-property-related expenses, discounted to a present value using an annual discount rate of 10% in accordance with the guidelines of the SEC.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Probable Reserves: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Reserves that are less certain to be recovered than proved reserves but that, together with proved reserves, are as likely as not to be recovered.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU5"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Producti</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">on costs: </font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Costs incurred to operate and maintain wells and related equipment and facilities, including depreciation and applicable operating costs of support equipment and facilities and other costs of operating and maintaining those wells and related equi</font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">pment and facilities. For a complete definition of production costs, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(20).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Productive well: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A well that is found to be capable of producing hydrocarbons in sufficient quantities such that proceeds from the sale of the production exceed production expenses and taxes.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Prospect: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A specific geographic area which, based on supporting geological, geophysical or other data and also preliminary economic analysis using reasonably anticipated prices and costs, is deemed to have potential for the discovery of commercial hydrocarbons.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Proved area: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Part of a property to which proved reserves have been specifically attributed.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Proved developed reserves: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Reserves that can be expected to be recovered through (i) existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared with the cost of a new well or (ii) through installed extraction equipment and infrastructure operational at the time of the reserves estimate if the extraction is by means not involving a well.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Proved properties: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Properties with proved reserves.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Proved reserves: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Those quantities of oil, natural gas and NGLs, which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible&#8212;from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods, and government regulations&#8212;prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within a reasonable time. For a complete definition of proved oil and natural gas reserves, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(22).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Proved undeveloped reserves or PUDs: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Proved reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion. Reserves on undrilled acreage are limited to those directly offsetting development spacing areas that are reasonably certain of production when drilled, unless evidence using reliable technology exists that establishes reasonable certainty of economic producibility at greater distances. Undrilled locations are classified as having undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless the specific circumstances justify a longer time. Under no circumstances are estimates for proved undeveloped reserves attributable to any acreage for which an application of fluid injection or other improved recovery technique is contemplated, unless such techniques have been proved effective by actual projects in the same reservoir or an analogous reservoir, or by other evidence using reliable technology establishing reasonable certainty.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Realized price: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The cash market price less all expected quality, transportation and demand adjustments.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reasonable certainty: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A high degree of confidence. For a complete definition of reasonable certainty, refer to the SEC&#8217;s Regulation S-X, Rule 4-10(a)(24).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recompletion: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The completion for production of an existing wellbore in another formation from that which the well has been previously completed</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reliable technology: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Reliable technology is a grouping of one or more technologies (including computational methods) that has been field tested and has been demonstrated to provide reasonably certain results with consistency and repeatability in the formation being evaluated or in an analogous formation.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reserves: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Estimated remaining quantities of oil and natural gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations. In addition, there must exist, or there must be a reasonable expectation that there will exist, the legal right to produce or a revenue interest in the production, installed means of delivering oil and natural gas or related substances to market and all permits and financing required to implement the project. Reserves should not be assigned to adjacent reservoirs isolated by major, potentially sealing, faults until those reservoirs are penetrated and evaluated as economically producible. Reserves should not be assigned to areas that are clearly separated from a known accumulation by a non-productive reservoir (i.e., absence of reservoir, structurally low reservoir or negative test results). Such areas may contain prospective resources (i.e., potentially recoverable resources from undiscovered accumulations).</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">4</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU6"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reservoir: </font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible oil and/or natural gas that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Resources: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Quantities of oil and natural gas estimated to exist in naturally occurring accumulations. A portion of the resources may be estimated to be recoverable and another portion may be considered to be unrecoverable. Resources include both discovered and undiscovered accumulations.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Royalty: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">An interest in an oil and natural gas lease that gives the owner the right to receive a portion of the production from the leased acreage (or of the proceeds from the sale thereof), but does not require the owner to pay any portion of the production or development costs on the leased acreage. Royalties may be either landowner&#8217;s royalties, which are reserved by the owner of the leased acreage at the time the lease is granted, or overriding royalties, which are usually reserved by an owner of the leasehold in connection with a transfer to a subsequent owner.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Spacing: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The distance between wells producing from the same reservoir. Spacing is often expressed in terms of acres, e.g., 40-acre spacing, and is often established by regulatory agencies.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Spot market price: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The cash market price without reduction for expected quality, transportation and demand adjustments.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Standardized measure: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Discounted future net cash flows estimated by applying year-end prices to the estimated future production of year-end proved reserves. Future cash inflows are reduced by estimated future production and development costs based on period-end costs to determine pre-tax cash inflows. Future income taxes, if applicable, are computed by applying the statutory tax rate to the excess of pre-tax cash inflows over our tax basis in the oil and natural gas properties. Future net cash inflows after income taxes are discounted using a 10% annual discount rate.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Undeveloped acreage: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Lease acreage on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production of commercial quantities of oil and natural gas regardless of whether such acreage contains proved reserves.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unproved properties: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Properties with no proved reserves.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Wellbore: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The hole drilled by the bit that is equipped for oil and natural gas production on a completed well. Also called well or borehole.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Working interest: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">The right granted to the lessee of a property to develop and produce and own natural gas or other minerals. The working interest owners bear the exploration, development and operating costs on either a cash, penalty or carried basis.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Workover: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">Operations on a producing well to restore or increase production.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WTI: <font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">West Texas Intermediate.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br /></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU7"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commonly Used Defined Terms</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As used in this Annual Report unless the context indicates or otherwise requires, the terms listed below have the following meanings:</p>

<div align="left">

<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We caution you that these forward-looking statements are subject to all of the risks and uncertainties, most of which are difficult to predict and many of which are beyond our control, incident to the development, production, gathering and sale of oil and natural gas. These risks include, but are not limited to, commodity price volatility, inflation, lack of availability of drilling and production equipment and services, environmental risks, drilling and other operating risks, regulatory changes, the uncertainty inherent in estimating reserves and in projecting future rates of production, cash flow and access to capital, the timing of development expenditures and the other risks described under &#8220;Item 1A. Risk Factors&#8221; included in this Annual Report.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reserve engineering is a process of estimating underground accumulations of oil and natural gas that cannot be measured in an exact way. The accuracy of any reserve estimate depends on the quality of available data, the interpretation of such data and price and cost assumptions made by reserve engineers. In addition, the results of drilling, testing and production activities may justify revisions of estimates that were made previously. If significant, such revisions would change the schedule of any further production and development program. Accordingly, reserve estimates may differ significantly from the quantities of oil and natural gas that are ultimately recovered.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Should one or more of the risks or uncertainties described in this Annual Report occur, or should underlying assumptions prove incorrect, our actual results and plans could differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements.</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="FIS_PART_I"></a><a name="WRD_10K_20161231_HTM_PART_I"></a><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU11"></a><a name="PART_I"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="PART_I"></a>PART</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> I</font></p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.06%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ITEM 1.</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><a name="ITEM_1_BUSINESS"></a><a name="ITEM_1_BUSINESS"></a>BUSINESS</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overview</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WildHorse Resource Development Corporation (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a Delaware corporation, the common stock, par value $0.01 per share, of which are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (&#8220;NYSE&#8221;) under the symbol &#8220;WRD.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;We completed our initial public offering on December 19, 2016.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We operate in one reportable segment engaged in the acquisition, exploitation, development and production of oil, natural gas and NGL resources. Our assets are characterized by concentrated acreage positions in East Texas and North Louisiana with multiple producing stratigraphic horizons, or stacked pay zones, and attractive single-well rates of return.&#160;In East Texas, we primarily operate in Burleson, Lee and Washington Counties where we primarily target the Eagle Ford Shale. In North Louisiana, we have historically operated in and around the highly prolific Terryville Complex, where we primarily targeted the overpressured Cotton Valley play. Following the NLA Divestiture (as defined below), our operations will be focused exclusively in East Texas, though all references to our assets and operations in this Annual Report do not give effect to the NLA Divestiture unless otherwise specified. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017, we had assembled a total leasehold position of approximately 585,941 gross (477,153 net) acres across our expanding acreage, including approximately 460,000 gross (387,091 net) acres in the Eagle Ford and approximately 125,941 gross (90,062 net) acres in North Louisiana.&#160;We have identified a total of approximately 6,069 gross (3,739 net) drilling locations across our acreage. For the year ended December 31, 2017, approximately 80%, 14% and 5% of our revenues were attributable to oil, natural gas and NGLs, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Developments</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Acquisition of Lee County Properties</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 1, 2018, we through our wholly owned subsidiary WHR Eagle Ford LLC (&#8220;WHR EF&#8221;), closed on our acquisition of producing and non-producing properties in Lee County, Texas for approximately $18.6 million from an undisclosed seller. The properties consist of approximately 17,500 net acres immediately contiguous to our existing Eagle Ford properties and one operated (four non-operated) producing horizontal wells. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pending Divestiture of North Louisiana Assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:5pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;On February 12, 2018, WHR II entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement with Tanos Energy Holdings III, LLC (&#8220;Tanos&#8221;) for the sale of all of our producing and non-producing oil and natural gas properties (including Oakfield), primarily located in Webster, Claiborne, Lincoln, Jackson and Ouachita Parishes, Louisiana (&#8220;NLA Assets&#8221;) for a total sales price of approximately $217.0&#160;million (the &#8220;NLA Divestiture&#8221;), subject to customary purchase price adjustments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The NLA Assets consist of all of our assets in our North Louisiana Acreage.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, WRD could receive contingent payments of up to $35.0 million based on the number of wells spud over the next four years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effective date of the proposed sale is January&#160;1, 2018, and we expect to close the transaction by the end of March 2018. The NLA Assets include approximately 90,000 net acres.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December&#160;31, 2017, estimated proved reserves from these properties were approximately 68.7 MMBoe, or 15% of our estimated year-end 2017 proved reserves. The sale includes approximately 620 gross (356.8 net) wells that produced approximately 7.2 MBoe/d (96% gas) for the year ended December&#160;31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our well count on these properties consisted of 473 gross (346.1 net) operated wells and 147 gross (10.7 net) non-operated wells.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The sales price is subject to adjustments for (i)&#160;operating expenses, capital expenditures and revenues between the effective date and the closing date, (ii)&#160;title, casualty and environmental defects, and (iii)&#160;other purchase price adjustments customary in oil and gas purchase and sale agreements. Pursuant to the terms of the Purchase and Sale Agreement, Tanos paid WHR II a deposit of $21.7&#160;million at signing, which amount will be applied to the sales price if the transaction closes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:5pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;The completion of the NLA Divestiture is subject to customary closing conditions. The parties may terminate the Purchase and Sale Agreement by mutual written consent or if certain closing conditions have not been satisfied, if total adjustments to the sales price exceed 20% of the sales price, or approximately $43&#160;million, or the transaction has not closed on or before April 30, 2018. If one or more of the closing conditions are not satisfied, or if the transaction is otherwise terminated, the divestiture may not be completed. There can be no assurance that we will sell the NLA Assets on the terms or timing described or at all. If the NLA Divestiture closes, we intend to use the net proceeds to repay amounts outstanding under our credit facility and for general corporate purposes. Please see Item 1A &#8220;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks Related to our Business&#8212;Our pending NLA Divestiture may not be consummated.&#8221;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Development of In-field Sand Mine</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU12"></a>On February 12, 2018, we announced that Burleson Sand LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary had previously acquired surface and sand rights on approximately 727 acres in Burleson County, Texas to construct and operate an in-field sand mine.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect that the </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">total capital expenditure for the full development of the sand mine will be approximately $65.0</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">- $75.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">0 million in 2018, which includes the property acquisition and third-party engineering studies.</font><font style="font-family:Calibri;font-size:11pt;margin-left:36pt;"></font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North Louisiana Settlement</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 1, 2018, we settled a dispute related to a possible area of mutual interest (&#8220;AMI&#8221;) associated with our North Louisiana properties with a third party.&#160; This settlement is referred to as the &#8220;North Louisiana Settlement.&#8221;&#160; See Note 21 under &#8220;Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8221; for additional information regarding the North Louisiana Settlement.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Tax Reform Legislation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, the United States ("U.S.") government enacted Public Law No. 115-97, commonly referred to as the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#8220;Tax Act&#8221;), which made significant changes to U.S. federal income tax law. We expect that certain aspects of these changes will positively impact our future after-tax earnings primarily due to the lower federal statutory income tax rate. We were required to recognize the effect of this rate change on our deferred tax assets and liabilities in 2017, the period the tax rate change was enacted. Key aspects of the Tax Act include, but are not limited to, (i) establishing a flat corporate income tax rate of 21% to replace previous rates that ranged from 15% to 35% and eliminating the corporate alternative minimum tax (&#8220;AMT&#8221;); (ii) reducing the maximum deduction for net operating loss (&#8220;NOL&#8221;) carryforwards arising in tax years beginning after December 31, 2017 to 80% of the taxpayer&#8217;s taxable income, allowing any NOLs generated in tax years beginning after&#160;December 31, 2017 to be carried forward indefinitely, and generally repealing carrybacks; (iii) limiting the deduction for net interest expense; (iv) allowing businesses to immediately expense the cost of new investments in certain qualified depreciable assets acquired after September 27, &#160;2017 (with a phase-down of such expensing starting in 2023); and (v) repealing the Section 199 domestic production deduction beginning in 2018.; The Tax Act did not include any changes with respect to the current option to expense Intangible Drilling Costs or the Percentage Depletion deduction. See Note 17 under &#8220;Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8221; for additional information regarding our income taxes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2017 Developments</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">APC/KKR Acquisition</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May 10, 2017, we, through our wholly owned subsidiary, WHR EF,&nbsp;&nbsp;entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement (the &#8220;First Acquisition Agreement&#8221;) by and among WHR EF, as purchaser, and Anadarko E&amp;P Onshore LLC (&#8220;APC&#8221;), Admiral A Holding L.P., TE Admiral A Holding L.P. and Aurora C-I Holding L.P. (collectively, &#8220;KKR&#8221; and, together with APC, the &#8220;First Sellers&#8221;), as sellers, to acquire certain acreage and associated production in Burleson, Brazos, Lee, Milam, Robertson and Washington Counties, Texas (the &#8220;Purchase&#8221;). Also on May 10, 2017, WHR EF entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement (together, with the First Acquisition Agreement, the &#8220;Acquisition Agreements&#8221;), by and among WHR EF, as purchaser, and APC and Anadarko Energy Services Company (together, with APC, the &#8220;APC Subs&#8221; and together with the First Sellers, the &#8220;Sellers&#8221;), as sellers, to acquire certain acreage and associated production in Burleson, Brazos, Lee, Milam, Robertson, and Washington Counties, Texas (together, with the Purchase, the &#8220;Acquisition&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pursuant to the Acquisition Agreements, on June 30, 2017, we completed the acquisition of approximately 111,000 acres and the associated production therefrom. The aggregate purchase price for the assets, as described in the Acquisition Agreements, consisted of an aggregate of approximately $533.6 million of cash to the APC Subs and approximately 5.5 million shares of our common stock valued at approximately $60.8 million to KKR. The common stock portion of the purchase price payable to KKR was issued pursuant to a Stock Issuance Agreement that was executed, on May 10, 2017, by and among us and KKR. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preferred Stock Issuance </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We partially funded the Acquisition through the issuance of 435,000 shares of Preferred Stock in exchange for $435.0 million on June 30, 2017, pursuant to a Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement (the &#8220;Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement&#8221;), by and among us and CP VI Eagle Holdings, L.P. (the &#8220;Carlyle Investor&#8221;), an affiliate of The Carlyle Group, L.P.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 10 under &#8220;Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8221; for additional information regarding our preferred stock issuance.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Amendments to Credit Agreement</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June&#160;30, 2017, the Company, each of the Company&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiaries (each as a guarantor), Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent (the &#8220;Administrative Agent&#8221;), and the lenders party thereto entered into a second amendment (the &#8220;Second Amendment&#8221;) to the Credit Agreement dated as of December&#160;19, 2016, among the Company, the Administrative Agent and the other agents and lenders party thereto (as amended, the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU13"></a><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Second Amendment, among other things, modified the Credit Agreement to (a)&#160;permit the Company to enter into the Acquisition, and the Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement, a</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nd perform its obligations under and in connection therewith, including the issuance of the Preferred Stock, (b)&#160;increase the Company&#8217;s borrowing base and elected commitment amount from $450 million to $650 million, (c)&#160;increase the annual cap on certain r</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">estricted payments from $50 million to $75 million, and (d)&#160;modify the definition of net debt so that certain contingent obligations, accounts payable, obligations to make deliveries in respect of advance payments, take or pay obligations, disqualified cap</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ital stock and obligations in respect of production payments are excluded from net debt for purposes of the Company&#8217;s leverage covenant.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On October 4, 2017, the Company, each of the Company&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiaries (each as a guarantor), the Administrative Agent, and the lenders party thereto entered into a Third Amendment (the &#8220;Third Amendment&#8221;) to the Credit Agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Third Amendment, among other things, modified the Credit Agreement to (i) increase the aggregate maximum credit amount to $2.0 billion from $1.0 billion, (ii) increase the borrowing base from $612.5 million to $875.0 million and (iii) add additional lenders.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2025 Senior Notes Offering</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 1, 2017, we completed a private placement of $350.0 million aggregate principal amount of 6.875% senior unsecured notes due 2025 (the &#8220;2025 Senior Notes&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2025 Senior Notes were issued at a price of 99.244% of par and resulted in net proceeds of approximately $338.6 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, on September 19, 2017, we completed another private placement of $150.0 million aggregate principal amount of the 2025 Senior Notes issued at 98.26% of par, which resulted in net proceeds of approximately $144.7 million. The notes issued in September 2017 are treated as a single class of debt securities with the 2025 Senior Notes issued in February 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp; The 2025 Senior Notes will mature on February 1, 2025 and interest is payable on February 1 and August 1 of each year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2025 Senior Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a joint and several basis by all of our existing and certain future subsidiaries (subject to customary release provisions).&nbsp;&nbsp;We have no material assets or operations that are independent of our existing subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp; There are no restrictions on our ability to obtain funds from our subsidiaries through dividends or loans.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net proceeds from each of the offerings of the 2025 Senior Notes were used to repay borrowings outstanding under our revolving credit facility and for general corporate purposes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pursuant to registration rights agreements entered into in connection with the offerings of the 2025 Senior Notes, we agreed to file a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) so that holders of the 2025 Senior Notes could exchange the unregistered 2025 Senior Notes for registered notes with substantially identical terms. In addition, we agreed to exchange the unregistered guarantees related to the 2025 Senior Notes for registered guarantees with substantially identical terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November 20, 2017, substantially all of the outstanding 2025 Senior Notes were exchanged for an equal principal amount of registered 6.875% senior notes due 2025 pursuant to an effective registration statement on Form S-4.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may redeem all or any part of the 2025 Senior Notes at a &#8220;make-whole&#8221; redemption price, plus accrued and unpaid interest, at any time before February 1, 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may also redeem up to 35% of the aggregate principal amount of the 2025 Senior Notes prior to February&#160;1, 2020 in an amount not greater than the net cash proceeds from one or more equity offerings at a redemption price of 106.875% of the principal amount of the 2025 Senior Notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Exercise of Underwriters&#8217; Over-allotment Option</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 17, 2017, we issued and sold 2,297,100 shares of our common stock at an offering price of $15.00 per share pursuant to the partial exercise of the underwriters&#8217; over-allotment option associated with our initial public offering (the &#8220;Option Exercise&#8221;). We received net proceeds of $32.6 million from the Option Exercise, all of which was used to repay outstanding borrowings under our revolving credit facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Properties</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Eagle Ford Acreage</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Eagle Ford Shale is one of the most active unconventional shale trends in North America.&#160;According to weekly rig count metrics published by Baker Hughes, the Eagle Ford Shale has consistently been one of the most active basins in the United States since 2011 and currently has the second highest rig count of all major U.S. basins.&#160;&#160;The Eagle Ford Shale trends across Texas from the Mexican border north into East Texas and is roughly 50 miles wide and 400 miles long. The Eagle Ford Shale rests between the Austin Chalk and the Buda Lime at a depth of approximately 4,000 to 14,000 feet. As of December 31, 2017, there were approximately 36,000 producing wells in the Eagle Ford with an average production of 2.1 MMBoe/d in December 2017.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We currently target a portion of the Eagle Ford Shale at depths between 6,000 feet and 13,000 feet primarily in Burleson, Lee, Brazos and Washington Counties, Texas. This portion of the Eagle Ford Shale averages 125 feet in thickness and contains 70% carbonate.&#160;We believe that the elevated carbonate percentages are in large part responsible for the brittleness of the Eagle Ford and successful completions which exhibit high productivity when fractured. The overall clay content of the Eagle Ford increases regionally as it continues progressively northeast into Brazos, Grimes and Madison Counties, Texas.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU14"></a><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> are focused on maximizing returns and expect operational efficiencies to extend beyond our existing drilling inventory to additional horizons. In addition, our acreage has been extensively developed for more than 40 years through the development of the Gi</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ddings Austin Chalk Trend. Based on analysis and interpretation of well results and other geologic and engineering data, we believe our acreage is also prospective for the Georgetown, Buda, Woodbine and Pecan Gap formations. Historical operators in the Gid</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">dings Austin Chalk Trend have experienced drilling and production success during </font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our industry&#8217;s pre-multistage frac era</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> (1970s-2000s). Future development results achieved by us and offset operators may allow us to expand our existing location inventory thr</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">oughout our leasehold.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We entered the Eagle Ford with the goal of redeveloping the area with horizontal drilling and modern completion techniques. Since that time, we have completed multiple bolt-on acquisitions and in-fill leases to build our current position in the Eagle Ford.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have identified a substantial inventory of 4,675 gross drilling locations within our Eagle Ford Acreage across Burleson, Brazos, Lee, Robertson and Washington Counties.&nbsp;&nbsp;The wells in our Eagle Ford Acreage have shown a strong track record of increasing EURs and a decreasing trend in drilling and completion capital costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017, our Eagle Ford position included approximately 387,091 net acres. Also, as of December 31, 2017, approximately 69% of our Eagle Ford Acreage was held by production, with an average working interest of 84%, and, as of December 31, 2017, 22% of our 385.6 MMBoe of proved reserves were developed, 88% of which were liquids. Since January 2014, we and our previous owner have drilled and completed 125 wells, acquired 878 wells and participated in 26 wells resulting in total net production of approximately 23.5 MBoe/d (76% oil, 10% natural gas and 14% NGLs), including non-operated production.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North Louisiana Acreage</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Within our North Louisiana Acreage we primarily target the overpressured Cotton Valley formation in the Terryville Complex. The Cotton Valley formation, extending across East Texas, North Louisiana and Southern Arkansas, has been under development since the 1930s and is characterized by thick, multi-zone natural gas and oil reservoirs with well-known geologic characteristics and long-lived, predictable production profiles. In 2005, operators started redeveloping the Cotton Valley using horizontal drilling and advanced hydraulic fracturing techniques.  Some large, analogous redevelopment projects in the Terryville Complex include the Terryville play in Lincoln Parish, the Nan-Su-Gail area in Freestone County, East Texas and the Carthage Complex in Panola County, East Texas.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our North Louisiana Acreage spans across the Webster, Claiborne, Bienville, Lincoln, Jackson and Ouachita Parishes, focusing on the Bear Creek field and the RCT and Weyerhaeuser Areas, where we are targeting overpressured Cotton Valley opportunities in multiple zones. We believe the Terryville Complex, which has been producing since 1954, is one of North America&#8217;s most prolific liquids rich natural gas plays, characterized by high recoveries relative to drilling and completion costs, high initial production rates with high liquids yields, long reserve life, multiple stacked pay zones, available infrastructure and a large number of service providers. The RCT Area is a direct offset of the Terryville Field and is part of the same Terryville Complex trend. Following the NLA Divestiture, we do not expect to continue operating in this area.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2017, our North Louisiana Acreage included approximately 90,000 net acres. Also, as of December 31, 2017, 58% of our acreage was then held by production, with an average working interest of 72%, and 41% of our 68.7 MMBoe of proved reserves were developed, 97% of which were natural gas. Since the inception of our predecessor, we had drilled and completed 18 wells, acquired 597 wells and participated in 5 non-operated wells resulting in a total 2017 net production of approximately 7.2 MBoe/d (2% oil, 96% natural gas and 2% NGLs), including non-operated production.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 12, 2018, WHR II entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement with Tanos for the sale of the NLA Assets for a total sales price of approximately $217.0&#160;million before customary adjustments. The NLA Divestiture is expected to close by the end of March 2018.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">13</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU15"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Reserve Summary</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our estimated proved reserves of were prepared by our internal reserve engineers and audited by Cawley, Gillespie and Associates, Inc. (&#8220;Cawley&#8221;), our independent reserve engineers.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2017, we had 454.3 MMBoe of estimated proved reserves.&#160;&#160;As of this date, our proved reserves were 75% oil and NGLs and 25% natural gas.&#160;&#160;The following table provides summary information regarding our estimated proved reserves data and our average net daily production by area based on our reserve reports as of December 31, 2017:</p>
