<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED AND COMBINED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-style:normal;">carryforw</font><font style="font-style:normal;">ards of approximately $1.0 million, which is not subject to expiration and will be refundable in tax years beginning after 2017 and before 2022.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company did not record a valuation allowance against its deferred tax assets including tax attributes base</font><font style="font-style:normal;">d upon management&#8217;s evaluation that it is more likely than not that the Company will realize its deferred tax assets.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="WRD_10K_20161231_HTM_NOTE_16_COMMITMENTS"></a><a name="NOTE_17_COMMITMENTS_CONTINGENCIES"></a><a name="NOTE_17_COMMITMENTS_CONTINGENCIES"></a>Note 18. Commitments and Contingencies</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigation &amp; Environmental</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are party to various ongoing and threatened legal actions relating to our entitled ownership interests in certain properties. We evaluate the merits of existing and potential claims and accrue a liability for any that meet the recognition criteria and can be reasonably estimated. We did not recognize any liability as of December 31, 2017 or 2016. Our estimates are based on information known about the matters and the input of attorneys experienced in contesting, litigating, and settling similar matters. Actual amounts could differ from our estimates and other claims could be asserted.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, we could be liable for environmental claims arising in the ordinary course of business. At December&#160;31, 2017 and 2016, no environmental obligations were recognized.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transportation</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dedicated Fracturing Fleet Services Agreements</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:8pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2017, we entered into two dedicated fracturing fleet services agreements to complete wells in a timely manner following conclusion of drilling operations in the Eagle Ford.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 15, 2017, we entered into a 20-month dedicated fracturing fleet services agreement. The agreement may be extended for an additional twelve months. We have agreed to pay a fixed monthly service fee of $2.7 million that covers equipment and personnel costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the fixed monthly service charge, we have agreed to pay a fixed fee for each stage completed in excess of 360 stages per calendar quarter.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have also agreed to pay a pass through fee for the cost of chemicals and fuel plus 10%.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have the right to terminate the contract with appropriate notice; however, an early termination fee of approximately $1.4 million times the number of months remaining under the initial term of the contract would be payable on such termination date. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F &#8211; 34</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WILDHORSE RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED AND COMBINED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU118"></a><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June 1, 2017, we entered into a 23-month dedicated fracturing fleet services agreement, which may be extended for an additional twelve months.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have agreed to pay a fixed monthly service fee</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> of $2.8 million that covers equipment and personnel costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we have agreed to pay a fixed fee for each stage completed in excess of 115 stages per month.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have also agreed to pay a pass through fee for the cost of chemicals and fuel plus 1</font><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">0%.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have the right to terminate the contract with appropriate notice; however an early termination fee of $1.4 million times the number of months remaining under the initial term of the contract would be payable on such termination date.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interruptible Water Availability Agreement</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company entered into an interruptible water availability agreement with the Brazos River Authority (&#8220;BRA&#8221;) that began on February 1, 2017 and ends on December 31, 2021.&nbsp;&nbsp;The agreement provides us with an aggregate of 6,978 acre-feet of water per year from the Brazos River at prices that may be adjusted periodically by BRA. The agreement requires annual payments to be made on or before February 15 of each year during the term of the agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;We recorded a payment of $0.4 million during the year ended December 31, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="WRD_10K_20161231_HTM_NOTE_17_QUARTERLY_F"></a><a name="NOTE_18_QUARTERLY_FINANCIAL_INFORMATION_"></a><a name="NOTE_18_QUARTERLY_FINANCIAL_INFORMATION_"></a>Note 19. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="WRD_10K_20161231_HTM_NOTE_18_SUPPLEMENTA"></a><a name="NOTE_19_SUPPLEMENTAL_OIL_GAS_INFORMATION"></a><a name="NOTE_19_SUPPLEMENTAL_OIL_GAS_INFORMATION"></a>Note 20. Supplemental Oil and Gas Information (Unaudited)</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Oil and Natural Gas Reserves</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Users of this information should be aware that the process of estimating quantities of &#8220;proved&#8221; and &#8220;proved developed&#8221; oil and natural gas reserves is very complex, requiring significant subjective decisions in the evaluation of all available geological, engineering and economic data for each reservoir. The data for a given reservoir may also change substantially over time as a result of numerous factors including, but not limited to, additional development activity, evolving production history and continual reassessment of the viability of production under varying economic conditions. As a result, revisions to existing reserve estimates may occur from time to time. Although every reasonable effort is made to ensure reserve estimates reported represent the most accurate assessments possible, the subjective decisions and variances in available data for various reservoirs make these estimates generally less precise than other estimates included in the financial statement disclosures.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU119"></a>Proved reserves are those quantities of oil and natural gas that by analysis of geoscience and engineering data can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible &#8212; from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations &#8212; prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F &#8211; 35</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED AND COMBINED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within a reasonable time.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our proved reserves are prepared by us and audited by Cawley, our independent reserve engineer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Proved reserves for 2016 were, with respect to WHR II, prepared by WHR II and audited by Cawley. With respect to Esquisto, the proved reserves were prepared by Cawley, its independent reserve engineer, for 2015.&#160;&#160;Esquisto&#8217;s proved reserves for 2016 were internally prepared and audited by Cawley.&#160;&#160;All proved reserves are located in the United States and all prices are held constant in accordance with SEC rules.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 3 for additional information on acquisitions and divestitures.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A variety of methodologies are used to determine our proved reserve estimates. The principal methodologies employed are reservoir simulation, decline curve analysis, volumetric, material balance, advance production type curve matching, petro-physics/log analysis and analogy. Some combination of these methods is used to determine reserve estimates in substantially all of our fields.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F &#8211; 37</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WILDHORSE RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED AND COMBINED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU121"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Standardized Measure of Dis</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">counted Future Net Cash Flows from Proved Reserves</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As required by the FASB and SEC, the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows presented below is computed by applying first-day-of-the-month average prices, year-end costs and legislated tax rates and a discount factor of 10 percent to proved reserves. We do not believe the standardized measure provides a reliable estimate of the Company&#8217;s expected future cash flows to be obtained from the development and production of its oil and gas properties or of the value of its proved oil and gas reserves. The standardized measure is prepared on the basis of certain prescribed assumptions including first-day-of-the-month average prices, which represent discrete points in time and therefore may cause significant variability in cash flows from year to year as prices change.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows is as follows:</p>

Subsequent Events</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lee County Acquisition</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 1, 2018, we, through our wholly owned subsidiary, WHR EF, closed its acquisition of producing and non-producing properties in Lee County, Texas for approximately $18.6 million from an undisclosed seller.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pending Divestiture of North Louisiana Assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;See Note 1&#8212;&#8220;Organization and Basis of Presentation&#8221; for additional information regarding the NLA Divestiture. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sand Mine Acquisition</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 4, 2018, Burleson Sand LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary, acquired surface and sand rights on approximately 727 acres in Burleson County, Texas for approximately $9.0 million to construct and operate an in-field sand mine.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Quarterly PIK Dividend</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">See Note 10&#8212;&#8220;Preferred Stock&#8221; for information regarding our quarterly PIK dividend.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">North Louisiana Settlement</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 1, 2018, we settled a dispute related to a possible area of mutual interest (&#8220;AMI&#8221;) associated with our North Louisiana assets with a third party.&#160; Pursuant to such settlement, the third party agreed to pay the actual net costs attributable to interests in certain leases and/or wells it elected to acquire.&#160; We agreed to provide the third party with a $7.0 million credit towards purchasing the interests selected by the third party, which is reflected in the accompanying statements of operations for the year ended&#160;December&#160;31, 2017 as &#8220;North Louisiana Settlement.&#8221;&#160; The settlement loss was partially offset by a tax benefit of $1.6 million.&#160; A settlement receivable of $5.9 million from the third party was also recognized by us.</p>
